questions.question: What is the primary definition of a 'model' in engineering?

options.A: A full-size product ready for market
options.C: A theoretical idea that cannot be tested
options.D: A marketing advertisement for a new product

questions.explanation: The lesson defines a model as simply a working representation of reality used to predict performance.

questions.question: In engineering, what does 'Ground Truth' refer to?

options.A: The initial design hypothesis before any testing
options.B: Objective data collected from a real-world physical system
options.C: The results of a computational simulation without physical verification
options.D: A historical record of past engineering failures

questions.explanation: Ground Truth is defined as objective data collected from a real-world physical system, providing definitive real-world information.

questions.question: What is the main purpose of 'Destructive Testing' with a physical model?

options.A: To preserve the model for future display
options.B: To intentionally push the model until it breaks or fails to find its limits
options.C: To make the model aesthetically pleasing for user feedback
options.D: To compare it with other models without causing any damage

questions.explanation: Destructive Testing involves intentionally pushing a model until it breaks to see its performance under extreme conditions and generate Ground Truth data.

questions.question: Why do engineers use both physical and computational models together to ensure integrity in their designs?

options.A: Computational models are always more accurate than physical ones, so physical models are secondary
options.B: Physical models provide Ground Truth data to validate the results of computational models
options.C: Physical models are only for aesthetic checks, while computational models handle all performance testing
options.D: It is faster and cheaper to build two different types of models than to rely on just one

questions.explanation: Engineers use both models because physical models provide the Ground Truth data necessary to validate the predictions made by computational models, ensuring integrity.

questions.question: How do models help engineers solve the 'Tradeoff' tension in design, such as balancing strength with cost?

options.A: Models eliminate the need for any compromises in design
options.B: Models provide objective data to find the optimal balance between conflicting objectives and constraints
options.C: Models force engineers to always choose the cheapest option regardless of other factors
options.D: Models only show how to make things stronger, not how to reduce weight or cost

questions.explanation: Models are the objective tool that provides data needed for discernment, helping engineers find the optimal solution to design tradeoffs like strength versus cost.

questions.question: If an engineer uses a 1:100 scaled model of a bridge, how does it help predict the performance of the full-size bridge?

options.A: The scaled model will perform exactly the same as the full-size bridge without any adjustments
options.B: The scaled model's performance is mathematically scaled up to predict the full-size system's behavior
options.C: The scaled model is only used for visual inspection and cannot provide performance data
options.D: A 1:100 scaled model is too small to provide any useful data for a large structure

questions.explanation: With a scaled model, the performance observed is mathematically scaled up to accurately predict how the full-size system will behave.

questions.question: A design team is creating a new ergonomic computer mouse. Which type of prototype would be best to quickly test how the mouse feels in a user's hand (User Experience) early in the design process?

options.A: A high-fidelity prototype made with final materials and electronics
options.B: A computational model simulating hand grip and comfort
options.C: A low-fidelity prototype made from simple materials like clay or cardboard
options.D: A full-size production model ready for mass manufacturing

questions.explanation: Low-fidelity prototypes, often made from simple materials, are used early in the design stage to check basic form, function, and aesthetics, including user experience.

questions.question: A bridge is designed to safely hold a maximum load of 50 tons. Through destructive testing, a physical model of the bridge fails at 200 tons. What is the Factor of Safety (FS) for this bridge design?
questions.explanation: The Factor of Safety (FS) is calculated by dividing the failure point (200 tons) by the maximum safe load (50 tons), which equals 4.

questions.question: An engineer is testing a new airplane wing design. To measure the internal forces of tension and compression within the wing material as it flexes during flight simulations, what instrument would be most appropriate?

options.C: A strain gauge to measure stretching and squeezing

questions.explanation: Strain gauges are specifically mentioned as instruments used to measure internal forces like tension and compression inside a material.

questions.question: The lesson states that 'validation' is checking if computational model results match physical model results (Ground Truth). How does this process connect to the biblical principle of truth and integrity?

options.A: It shows that only physical evidence is truly reliable, making computational models untrustworthy
options.B: It emphasizes the importance of verifying predictions with objective reality, similar to seeking verifiable truth
options.C: It suggests that engineers should always trust their initial hypotheses without needing external verification
options.D: It proves that human intuition is always superior to scientific data in design

questions.explanation: Validation connects to biblical truth and integrity by demonstrating the importance of verifying theoretical predictions (computational models) against objective, real-world evidence (Ground Truth).

questions.question: Which of the following statements accurately describe the role or characteristics of engineering models?

options.A: They are working representations of reality used to predict performance.
options.B: They eliminate the need for any compromises or tradeoffs in design.
options.C: They provide objective data to help engineers balance conflicting design goals.
options.D: They are always full-size products ready for market.

questions.explanation: Based on the lesson, models are working representations of reality that predict performance and provide objective data to manage design tradeoffs.

questions.question: Why do engineers often use both physical and computational models together in their design process?

options.A: Computational models are always more accurate than physical models, making physical models unnecessary.
options.B: Physical models generate objective Ground Truth data from real-world systems.
options.C: Computational models are primarily for aesthetic checks, while physical models handle all performance testing.
options.D: Ground Truth data from physical models is essential for validating the results of computational models.

questions.explanation: Physical models provide Ground Truth data from the real world, which is then used to validate and ensure the accuracy of computational models.

questions.question: A ___ is an instrument used to measure internal forces like stretching and squeezing (tension and compression) within a material.
questions.explanation: Strain gauges are specifically used to measure internal forces such as tension and compression within materials.

questions.question: Put these steps for validating a computational model using a physical model in the correct order.
items: Develop a computational model to make predictions.
Construct a physical model of the design.
Conduct destructive testing on the physical model to gather Ground Truth data.
Compare computational model results with Ground Truth data for validation.
questions.explanation: The process involves first creating a computational model, then building a physical model to generate real-world Ground Truth data through testing, and finally using that data to validate the computational model's predictions.
